distinguishing_features: Embeds a porous metallic foam wick within the bond coat as a lateral heat spreader that redistributes the TBC/BC interfacial thermal gradient
Uses a high-conductivity internal structure to lower peak interfacial temperature rather than changing insulation, chemistry, or monitoring
Deposits the foam via existing thermal spray/EBPVD coating-line modification, no new sensors or controls
Mitigates oxidation kinetics and CTE mismatch stress by reducing the driving peak temperature at the interface
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to reduce the peak bond-coat/ceramic interfacial temperature during transient thermal cycling so as to slow oxidation kinetics and lower CTE mismatch strain, without changing insulation, coating chemistry, or adding monitoring hardware.
parsed.viable_reason: A porous metallic foam wick embedded in the oxide/ceramic interface would itself oxidize and lacks a demonstrated thermal benefit, and the claimed 20-30% peak reduction and 2.5-3x oxidation reduction are asserted without valid supporting calculation.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Introducing an internal lateral heat-spreader structure to redistribute the TBC/BC thermal gradient is not a routine application of any of the cited monitoring, duty-cycle, or envelope-restriction approaches.
